newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries steady, little movement expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady, little movement expected.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities were steady Monday amid very light trading.

With no economic data releases due this session, traders said no substantive price movement was expected ahead of the release of the Employment Cost Index for the second quarter on Tuesday. The next potentially market moving data were second quarter Gross Domestic Product estimates on Wednesday and July nonfarm payrolls on Friday.
"The market's dead. There will be nothing going on until we see some numbers telling us where the economy is going," said a trader at a primary dealership.
Aside from the ECI and jobless claims numbers, new home sales were slated for release on Tuesday and the Chicago and New York purchasing managers surveys on Thursday.
June factory orders and personal income and consumption data were set for release on Friday.

Yields on the Treasury's 30-year bond remained below 6.50 percent as market participants were reassured the economy was in healthy shape after remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony last week in biannual Humphrey-Hawkins hearings. He hinted that further tightening was not needed in the immediate future, U.S experts said.

"I don't see the ECI or GDP reports being sharply higher and consumer spending doesn't seem to have risen enough (to raise concern)," said Cary Leahey, chief U.S. economist at High Frequency Economics.
Leahey said the market was wondering if there was a major acceleration in the ECI and said some short-covering could occur after home sales data were released on Wednesday.
But Leahey saw little occurring for the remainder of Monday's session.
Analysts said the bond market would see little price movement before major economic releases this week.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading 8/32 higher at 102-15 to yield 6.44 percent.
The three-month bill was one basis point lower at 5.09 percent. The six-month bill was unchanged at 5.14 percent and the year bill was one basis point lower at 5.22 percent.
The five-year note was up 1/32 at 99-23/32 to yield 6.07 percent, while the 10-year note was up 4/32 at 103-11/32 to yield 6.16 percent.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663 ))
